gloss: lip; speech, language; edge, rim, shore
summary: The lip, and from it what the lips do and what is shaped like a lip. A man's lips move when he speaks (1Sa 1:13) and are the organ of his speech: what goes out of the lips is a vow to be kept (Deu 23:24), lips of truth stand for ever and lips of falsehood are an abomination to Yahweh (Pro 12:19, 22), and a people may honour Yahweh with their lips while their heart is far from him (Isa 29:13, quoted by Jesus, Mat 15:8). A people's lip is its language: the whole earth had one lip at Babel until Yahweh confused it (Gen 11:1–9), and he will turn to the peoples a pure lip to call on his name (Zep 3:9). The lip of the sea, a river or a vessel is its shore, bank or rim, the sand on the lip of the sea that cannot be counted (Gen 22:17; Heb 11:12). Akkadian šaptu, Ugaritic špt, Arabic šafa and the Aramaic and Syriac siptā are the same word, and Akkadian šaptu has the same three sides: lip, word, edge or bank.

words.gloss: lip; speech; language; edge, rim, shore, bank
words.summary: 176 times, most often in the dual שְׂפָתַיִם “the (two) lips” of speech, above all in Proverbs and Psalms; the singular construct שְׂפַת is the edge of the sea, a river, a curtain or a vessel, and in Genesis 11 and the prophets a people's language. The lips are named with the mouth (פֶּה) and the tongue (לָשׁוֹן) and set against the heart.

senses.definition: The lips of the mouth: what moves when one speaks, is red or sweet in the Song, is touched or cleansed, and holds a bit put into it.

evidence.note: Hannah “was speaking in her heart; only her lips (שְׂפָתֶיהָ) moved, and her voice was not heard”.
“Like a thread of scarlet are your lips (שִׂפְתֹתַיִךְ), and your mouth is lovely.”
“Your lips drip honey, my bride; honey and milk are under your tongue.”
To Sennacherib: “I will put my hook in your nose and my bit in your lips (בִּשְׂפָתֶיךָ).” Also Isa 37:29.
“At the sound my lips quivered.”
The coal touched Isaiah's mouth: “Behold, this has touched your lips, and your iniquity is taken away.”
“One in the likeness of the sons of man touched my lips, and I opened my mouth and spoke.”
Those who see him “open wide with the lip, they shake the head”.

senses.gloss: lips as the organ of speech; what one says
senses.definition: The lips as what speaks, and so the speech itself: a vow or an oath that goes out of them, words true or false, praise, and mere talk set against the heart or against deeds.

evidence.note: “What has gone out of your lips (מוֹצָא שְׂפָתֶיךָ) you shall keep and do, as you have vowed to Yahweh … what you have spoken with your mouth.”
A woman's vows “or the rash utterance of her lips (מִבְטָא שְׂפָתֶיהָ) by which she bound herself”.
One who swears “speaking rashly with the lips”.
“I will not profane my covenant, nor alter what has gone out of my lips.”
“Lord, open my lips (שְׂפָתַי), and my mouth shall declare your praise.”
“With lips of joyful shouting my mouth shall praise you.”
“A lip of truth (שְׂפַת אֱמֶת) shall be established for ever, but a tongue of falsehood only for a moment.”
“Lips of falsehood are an abomination to Yahweh, but those who deal faithfully are his delight.”
“Keep your tongue from evil and your lips from speaking deceit”: quoted at 1Pe 3:10.
“Let him keep his tongue from evil and his lips (χείλη; Peshitta סֵפְוָתֵהּ) from speaking deceit.”
“The venom of a viper is under their lips”: quoted at Rom 3:13.
“The venom of asps is under their lips (χείλη; Peshitta סֵפְוָתְהוֹן).”
“This people draw near with their mouth and honour me with their lips (וּבִשְׂפָתָיו), but their heart is far from me”: lips set against the heart.
Jesus quotes Isa 29:13 of the Pharisees: “This people honours me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.” Also Mrk 7:6.
“You say, but it is only a word of lips (דְּבַר־שְׂפָתַיִם), ‘counsel and strength for war’”: empty talk. Also Isa 36:5.
“In all toil there is profit, but the word of lips leads only to want.”
“In all this Job did not sin with his lips.”
“He who restrains his lips is prudent.”
“Set a guard, Yahweh, over my mouth; keep watch over the door of my lips.”
“Iniquity was not found on his lips … the lips of a priest should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law from his mouth.”
Moses: “I am uncircumcised of lips (עֲרַל שְׂפָתָיִם); how then shall Pharaoh hear me?” Also Exo 6:30.
“I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips.”
“May Yahweh cut off all smooth lips … who say, With our tongue we will prevail; our lips are our own.”
“We will render bulls, our lips”: praise as the offering; Heb 13:15 “the fruit of lips confessing his name”.
“A sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips (καρπὸν χειλέων; Peshitta פִּארֵא דְּסֵפְוָתָא) confessing his name.”
Yahweh “creating the fruit of the lips: Peace, peace to the far and to the near”.
The shoot of Jesse “shall strike the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips he shall slay the wicked”.
Of Yahweh: “his lips are full of indignation, and his tongue is like a devouring fire”.

senses.definition: The speech a people shares and others do not understand: the one language of the earth before Babel, the language of Canaan, a foreign tongue, and the pure lip Yahweh will give the peoples.

evidence.note: “The whole earth was of one lip (שָׂפָה אֶחָת) and of the same words.”
“Behold, one people, and one lip for them all.”
“Let us go down and confuse their lip there, that they may not understand (יִשְׁמְעוּ) one another's lip.”
“Therefore its name was called Babel, because there Yahweh confused (בָּלַל) the lip of all the earth.”
“Five cities in the land of Egypt speaking the lip of Canaan (שְׂפַת כְּנַעַן) and swearing to Yahweh of armies.”
In Egypt “I heard a lip that I did not know”.
“With stammering of lip (בְּלַעֲגֵי שָׂפָה) and with another tongue he will speak to this people”: quoted at 1Co 14:21.
“In the law it is written, With men of other tongues and with other lips (ἐν χείλεσιν ἑτέροις) I will speak to this people”: Isa 28:11, of speaking in tongues.
“A people deep of lip, that you cannot hear, of a stammering tongue that you cannot understand.”
“Not to a people deep of lip (עִמְקֵי שָׂפָה) and heavy of tongue are you sent … whose words you cannot understand.”
“Then I will turn to the peoples a pure lip (שָׂפָה בְרוּרָה), that all of them may call on the name of Yahweh and serve him with one shoulder.”
“You have been taken up on the lip of the tongue (שְׂפַת לָשׁוֹן)”: the talk of the nations.

senses.definition: The lip of a thing: the shore of the sea, the bank of a river or wadi, the rim of a cup or the bronze sea, the hem of a curtain or the edge about the neck of the high priest's robe.

evidence.note: “I will multiply your seed … as the sand that is on the lip of the sea (עַל־שְׂפַת הַיָּם).” Heb 11:12 quotes it.
“As the sand which is by the lip of the sea (παρὰ τὸ χεῖλος τῆς θαλάσσης; Peshitta סֵפְתֵהּ דְּיַמָּא), innumerable.”
Camels “as the sand on the lip of the sea for multitude”.
Solomon's breadth of heart “as the sand on the lip of the sea”.
“Israel saw Egypt dead on the lip of the sea.”
Ezion-geber “on the lip of the Sea of Reeds”.
The cows came up out of the Nile “and stood by the other cows on the lip of the river (עַל־שְׂפַת הַיְאֹר)”.
The ark of papyrus set “in the reeds on the lip of the river”.
Elisha “stood on the lip of the Jordan”.
“One on this lip of the river, and one on that lip of the river.”
“By the river, on its lip, on this side and that, shall grow every tree for food … its leaf for healing.” Also Ezk 47:6–7.
“Aroer, which is on the lip of the wadi Arnon.”
“To the lip of Abel-meholah”: a border.
The bronze sea “ten cubits from its lip to its lip (מִשְּׂפָתוֹ עַד־שְׂפָתוֹ)”: its rim.
“Its lip was like the work of the lip of a cup (שְׂפַת־כּוֹס), a lily blossom.”
Loops of blue “on the lip of the one curtain at the end of the set”: its edge.
The robe's head-opening “shall have a lip (שָׂפָה) around its opening … that it not be torn”: a hem or binding. Also Exo 39:23.
The altar's border “to its lip all around”.

evidence.locator: Gen.11.1, 6, 9; Gen.22.17; Exo.14.30; Psa.34.14; Psa.140.4; Isa.28.11; Isa.29.13; Hos.14.3, שָׂפָה → χεῖλος; χεῖλος renders שָׂפָה ×120

evidence.note: “This people honours me with their lips (τοῖς χείλεσιν)”: Isa 29:13.
“The fruit of lips”, after Hos 14:3.
“Other lips”: Isa 28:11, the lip as a language.
“The lip of the sea”: Gen 22:17, the shore.

parallels.note: “Tongue”: lips and tongue together speak, truly or with deceit, and a foreign people is deep of lip and heavy of tongue.
“Mouth”: the lips open and the mouth declares; the people draw near with mouth and lips.

opposites.note: “Heart”: honour with the lips while the heart is far away; burning lips over an evil heart; the lips moving while one speaks in the heart.

phrases.gloss: what goes out of the lips: a word given, a vow
a word of lips: mere talk
uncircumcised of lips: unable to speak well

words.summary: Five times, always as what is covered or left untrimmed: the leper covers it and cries “Unclean”, the mourner and the shamed seer cover it, and Mephibosheth left it untended while David was in exile. The ־ָם ending is added to שָׂפָה; the upper lip with its hair.

senses.gloss: moustache, upper lip (covered in uncleanness, mourning or shame)
senses.definition: The hair of the upper lip, or the upper lip itself; to cover it (עָטָה עַל־שָׂפָם) is the sign of one unclean, mourning or put to shame, who does not speak or is not answered.

evidence.note: The leper's clothes torn, his head bare, “and he shall cover over the upper lip (וְעַל־שָׂפָם יַעְטֶה) and cry, Unclean, unclean”.
Ezekiel forbidden to mourn his wife: “you shall not cover over the upper lip, nor eat the bread of men”: the mourner's sign. Also Ezk 24:22.
“The seers shall be ashamed … and they shall all cover over the upper lip, for there is no answer of God.”
Mephibosheth “had not dressed his feet nor trimmed his moustache (שְׂפָמוֹ) nor washed his clothes” from the day David left: a moustache, tended or not.

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܣܦܬܐ (septā), plural ܣܦܘܬܐ (sep̄wāṯā), for χεῖλος in every verse where the New Testament quotes the Hebrew שָׂפָה, and for στόμα in Luk 6:45.

senses.definition: The lips that speak, honour, or hide venom, as the Hebrew שְׂפָתַיִם.

evidence.note: “This people honours me with its lips (בְּסֵפְוָתֵהּ), but their heart is far from me”: Isa 29:13. Also Mrk 7:6.
“From the abundance of the heart the lips (סֵפְוָתָא) speak”, where the Greek has “his mouth”.
“The venom of the asp is under their lips”: Psa 140:4.
“The fruit of lips (פִּארֵא דְּסֵפְוָתָא) that confess his name.”
“Let his lips not speak deceit”: Psa 34:14.

senses.definition: The lip of the sea, as the Hebrew שְׂפַת הַיָּם.

evidence.note: “As the sand on the lip of the sea (סֵפְתֵהּ דְּיַמָּא) that has no number”: Gen 22:17.

cognates.gloss: lip; word; edge, rim, bank, crest
cognates.note: Akkadian has all three sides of the Hebrew in the one word: the lip, the word spoken, and the edge or bank of a thing.

evidence.note: bank; crest; crest (of a wall); edge; lip; rim; word (×652).

cognates.note: In KTU 1.23 “their lips are sweet”; and in the Baal texts “from her lips her utterance”, the lips as what speaks, beside the mouth.

evidence.locator: p. 203, §93 Glossary, špt (KTU 1.23:49, 50 = 88.2) (OCR; page from the neighbouring entries špḥ and tk)
evidence.note: “špt /šapat-/: du. špthm 1.23:49, 50 = 88.2 ‘lip’ (H. šapa, Syr. septa, Arab. šapat, Akkad. šaptu).”

cognates.gloss: lip; (bint šafa) a word; (šafat an-nās) people's speaking of one, report
cognates.note: The lip of a man, and by it speech: “I spoke not to him a daughter of a lip”, a single word; and a man's šafa among the people is his good report, what they say of him. The verb šāfaha is to speak to another lip to lip.

evidence.note: “The lip of a human being … بِنْتُ شَفَةٍ A word … لَهُ فِينَا شَفَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ He has a good report … How good is the people's speaking of thee!”
“He spoke to him putting his lip near to his lip … the talking with another mouth to mouth.”

cognates.note: Lane equates شَفَا البِئْرِ and شَفَتُهَا, the lip and the brink of a well, both its edge: the Hebrew's lip of the sea and of a river.

evidence.locator: p. 1575, art. شفو and شفى, شَفًا (n22681)
evidence.note: “The point or extremity, verge, brink, or edge, of anything; like شَفَةٌ; for شَفَا الحُفْرَةِ … and شَفَتُهَا both signify the same.”

cognates.note: The Targums' word for שָׂפָה, both the hem of the tabernacle curtains (Targ. O. Exo 26:4) and the lip of speech (Targ. Pro 12:19, Psa 120:2).

evidence.note: “= h. שָׂפָה. 1) border, hem. Targ. O. Ex. XXVI, 4; 10 … 2) lip. Targ. Ps. LXXXI, 6 … Ib. CXX, 2 … Targ. Prov. XII, 19.”

evidence.locator: lexeme 2190, SITA (root 1308), lip; edge; margin; shore
evidence.note: The Syriac septā of the Peshitta.

cognates.note: The Targums keep the word in all four verses of the Hebrew's covering the upper lip, and once use it for a border (Targ. Y. I Exo 28:32), as שָׂפָה is.

evidence.note: “1) same [upper lip]. Targ. Lev. XIII, 45 … Targ. II Sam. XIX, 25 … Targ. Ez. XXIV, 17; 22. Targ. Mic. III, 7 … 2) border. Targ. Y. I Ex. XXVIII, 32.”

cognates.gloss: (Sabaic verb) promise; of a god, decree
cognates.note: Old South Arabian, where the noun “lip” is not attested: a verb “promise”, which the dictionary takes as formed from the lip, as a word given; compare the Hebrew מוֹצָא שְׂפָתַיִם, the vow that goes out of the lips.

evidence.note: “(1) PROMISE; of a god, perhaps DECREE … [Prob denom from the biradical n *śft ‘lip’ (not attested in Sab …)].” J698/9: “as his father had promised”.

doctrine.statement: At Babel “the whole earth was of one lip” and said, “let us make a name for ourselves”; Yahweh said that with one people and one lip nothing they planned would be withheld from them, and he confused their lip and scattered them (Gen 11:1, 4, 6–9). Zephaniah foretells the day when Yahweh gathers the nations to pour out his indignation on them, and then, “I will turn to the peoples a pure lip, that all of them may call on the name of Yahweh and serve him with one shoulder” (Zep 3:8–9). Isaiah sees cities of Egypt speaking “the lip of Canaan” and swearing to Yahweh, and Egypt, Assyria and Israel blessed together in the midst of the earth (Isa 19:18, 24–25). From the verses: the division of the nations' speech that began at Babel will be undone on the earth, not by men making a name for themselves but by Yahweh after his judgment on the nations, when the peoples call on his name with one lip.

Isaiah's shoot from the stem of Jesse, on whom the spirit of Yahweh rests, “shall strike the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips (בְּרוּחַ שְׂפָתָיו) he shall slay the wicked”, and then the earth shall be full of the knowledge of Yahweh (Isa 11:1–4, 9). Paul uses Isaiah's words of the Lord Jesus at his coming: the lawless one “whom the Lord shall consume with the breath of his mouth and destroy with the appearing of his coming” (2Th 2:8). From the verses: the judgment on the wicked that Isaiah gives to the son of David is carried out by Jesus when he returns, by the word of his lips, and it opens the age when the earth is full of the knowledge of Yahweh.

note: Drafted 2026-11-19. Words: שָׂפָה (u.bw.ab, 176) and שָׂפָם (u.bw.ac, 5). Left out: מִשְׂפָּח (m.dr.av, 0 tokens here), which the brief lists only as a cross-reference to root שׂפח (Isa 5:7); it belongs to that root. Added the Peshitta's ܣܦܬܐ as a syc word (SEDRA lexeme 2190, 7 tokens: Mat 15:8; Mrk 7:6; Luk 6:45; Rom 3:13; Heb 11:12; 13:15; 1Pe 3:10); its root key ספה is a guess (SEDRA's root is SITA ܣܦܬܐ) and should be checked. No personal names from the root. Sounds: sin is its own letter, so no `sounds`; Arabic š, Ugaritic š, Akkadian š and Aramaic s all agree with one older sound. The edge sense keeps its own Arabic cognate شَفًا (root شفو), which Lane equates with شَفَة of a well's brink; whether شفو and شفه are one root in Arabic is not settled here. Open questions: (1) Segert's page for špt (p. 203) is inferred from the OCR order, not read off the scan; (2) the Sabaic ŚFT “promise” is kept as possible; (3) Wiktionary links Classical Syriac ܦܣܡܐ “moustache” to שָׂפָם; not followed (it would need metathesis) and not recorded; (4) Ge'ez (Dillmann, Leslau) and Payne Smith not consulted. LXX γλῶσσα renders the language sense at Psa 81:6, Pro 17:4 and Zep 3:9; not recorded, as no New Testament verse quotes those.
